messages:
incident-bot: Paging @oncall (sev=2) for dedicated-us-east-2 pool: automated detectors flagged possible cross-tenant context leakage via prefix cache collisions. 5 anomalous responses observed referencing mismatched tenant_id. Thread auto-created for live coordination.

maya.patel: Ack. Oncall here. Pulling logs and contacting customer rep. @customer-503-escalation can you paste an example?

customer-503-escalation: Were seeing fragments of another tenant's prompt context inside completions. Not auth tokens but definitely other customer's domain content. Frequency ~1/10k requests. Very concerning for compliance.

alex.chen: I replayed a snippet in a staging replica with the same routing version. Reproducible when a routing snapshot and prefix cache update happen concurrently. Looks like prefix hash -> tenant mapping sometimes resolves to the wrong tenant shard. Attaching trace below.

alex.chen: Trace excerpt:
```
[2026-03-14T21:12:03Z] router-3 pid=2145 req=rcv-9a2f tenant=acme-health prefix_hash=0x7b2a shard=21 cached_prefix_tenant=bespoke-inc
[2026-03-14T21:12:03Z] router-3 WARN prefix_mismatch req=rcv-9a2f action=serve_from_cache
[2026-03-14T21:12:03Z] router-3 TRACE kv_get key=kv:prefix:0x7b2a -> tenant=bespoke-inc value_len=482
```

samir.khan: Confirmed. Root cause hypothesis: cache key composition omits tenant scope during a transitional snapshot write path. When routing snapshot writer flushes, it can overwrite a shared prefixDB without tenant locking. Race window small but high enough over steady traffic.

jess.ramos: Impact summary: Customer-503 (AcmeHealth) saw intermittent cross-tenant content; no creds seen so far but the content could contain sensitive prompt data. Recommend treating as potential exposure and escalating to SOC/legal.

maya.patel: Immediate mitigation plan (applied live):
- Disable prefix caching on all routers in dedicated-us-east-2: `runtime.kv.prefix_cache.enabled=false`.
- Evict existing prefix cache files and restart routers in the pool, one at a time, with health checks.
- Temporarily pin tenant->shard routing to bypass cache path for enterprise VPCs.

alex.chen: Commands being executed now on control plane:
```
# patch runtime config for pool
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/configs/router?pool=dedicated-us-east-2 -d '{"runtime.kv.prefix_cache.enabled": false}'

# evict and restart sample router
ssh router-3.example.internal sudo systemctl restart redwood-router
```

ops-sre: Rolling restart across 8 routers in pool. One-by-one, 30s healthcheck wait. If any restart fails, we roll back the config change for that router and escalate.

incident-bot: Update: config patch applied to 4/8 routers. Observed anomaly rate drop from ~1/10k to ~1/40k in next 15 minutes.

samir.khan: Forensics: preserving cache blobs and routing snapshots for postmortem analysis. Creating secure archive and snapshotting RocksDB store for correlation. Paths of interest:
- /var/lib/redwood/router/prefixdb.*
- /var/log/redwood/router/route-snapshots/*.json
- s3://secure-archives/incidents/incident-1773522540/

jess.ramos: Communications: drafting a customer-safe notification: describe what happened, list immediate mitigations taken, call out preserved artifacts, and commit to a timeline for root-cause and fix. Will run draft by legal/SOC before sending.

maya.patel: Short-term next steps:
1) Finish router restarts and confirm anomaly rate near zero.
2) Push code change to include tenant_id in prefix cache key so namespace can't collide.
3) Add canary for config rollout that simulates snapshot flush under load.

alex.chen: Proposed code snippet for cache key (sketch):
```
// include tenant in cache key to prevent cross-tenant collisions
std::string prefix_cache_key(const std::string &tenant_id, const std::string &prefix_hash) {
  return fmt::format("tenant:{}:prefix:{}", tenant_id, prefix_hash);
}
```

incident-bot: Pager handoff in 35 minutes to @oncall-nextshift. Current oncall: @maya.patel -> next: @samir.khan.

maya.patel: Handoff notes (@samir.khan):
- Disabled prefix cache for pool; 5/8 restarts complete.
- Artifacts archived: s3://secure-archives/incidents/incident-1773522540/
- Customer notified privately. Legal/SOC looped in.
- Metrics to watch: `kv.prefix_shadowing.rate`, `router.prefix_mismatch.count`, `customer.503.error_reports`.

samir.khan: I'll take next shift. Priority: finish restarts, validate rollback paths, keep preserving forensic blobs. I'll own the follow-up postmortem and remediation PR (include concurrency tests).

jess.ramos: Draft timeline for customer: initial notification within 1 hour, technical write-up and root-cause ETA 72 hours, code fix + staged rollout ETA 3 business days, final remediation report after postmortem. Updating customer rep.

customer-503-escalation: Appreciate the quick action. Please confirm when the pool is fully restarted and we can get the technical write-up for our security team.

maya.patel: ETA for completing restarts ~25 minutes. Will post updates here and in the private customer thread.

incident-bot: Automated note: anomaly rate trending downward. Escalation: active. All operator actions are being logged to the incident audit trail.

samir.khan: Marking for postmortem. I'll open remediation PR with unit and load tests that exercise concurrent snapshot writers and tenant-scoped cache keys. Tagging @eng-runtime for review in case runtime batching interacts with prefix writes.

maya.patel: leaving handoff. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

(END OF THREAD)
